A
The time-domain representation, like a waveform, plots the signal's amplitude against time. The frequency-domain representation, like a spectrum, is created by applying a Fourier Transform and shows the amplitude of each individual frequency that makes up the signal.

C
The Fourier Transform's primary purpose is to decompose a signal (like an audio wave) from its time-domain representation into its individual frequency components, revealing what frequencies are present and their respective amplitudes.

B
A frequency-domain representation, like a Fourier transform, shows the amplitude of the different frequencies that make up a signal. A simple oscillating signal consists of a single frequency, so it appears as a sharp peak or a vertical line at that specific frequency on the graph.

B
The Fourier Transform decomposes a complex signal into its constituent sine and cosine waves, showing the specific amplitude and phase of each frequency component required to reconstruct the original signal.

B
The Fourier Transform is a mathematical tool used to break down a signal (like an audio wave) into its constituent frequencies. This allows for the identification and filtering of specific frequencies, which is the basis for noise cancellation and for recognizing the unique frequency patterns of specific sounds or words.
